transcript: Here are three ways that Hell's Kitchen is completely redefining the genre of the bio-jukebox musical. The first thing, right off the bat you'll notice is that this show is called Hell's Kitchen. It is not called Hell's Kitchen: the Alicia Keys Story, and in fact the main character is not even Alicia Keys, it is a character called Ali. And so you may be thinking, “Ben if the main character isn't even Alicia Keys why are you calling it a bio jukebox musical?“ and that's because the character of Ali is heavily inspired by Alicia Keys and her childhood growing up in Hell's Kitchen with a single mother, an estranged father, learning to play piano, all of which we see the character of Ali doing. Now all bio jukebox musicals make things up for the sake of the story, and I kinda like the honesty of this one saying “Yes, we're inspired by Alicia Keys's childhood but we are not a direct 1:1” You may also notice that I've only mentioned Alicia Keys's childhood and that is because another smart thing that the show does is it focuses in on a small part of Alicia Keys's life, rather than trying to tell her entire life story. Part of the reason why bio-jukebox musicals have started to feel so stale, at least for me, is because they all kind of tell the same story: You start with the artist when they're younger, just starting out in the industry, and then you follow their career all the way through to them as an adult as the artist that we know them as today. By just focusing in on her childhood, you break free from that formula and it also gives you more time to really get to develop these characters because you're not rushing from scene to scene, trying to cram 60 years of history into 2.5 hours. You're just trying to cram in one year, which is much more manageable. And finally, I've seen a lot of confusion over whether this is a true jukebox musicals or whether Alicia Keys wrote original music for this show. I’m not sure if those three were written specifically for this musical or if they're just old Alicia Keys demos that they found and repurposed, but either way I think it's really smart to bring in new Alicia Keys material to help tell the story better rather than being reliant on just the existing catalogue of her greatest hits.
